intro: Picture waking up, pulling back the curtains, and seeing a sea of mist drifting over terraced tea plantations, the air crisp and cold, then walking up to sip a hot coffee at a 360° dining viewpoint — Phumektawan Resort is a small resort on Doi Mae Salong (Santikhiri), in Mae Salong Nok subdistrict, Mae Fa Luang district, Chiang Rai province, at an altitude of around 1,300 meters · what people talk about most is the mountain views and morning sea of mist, paired with a restaurant that looks out in every direction, with cool comfortable weather nearly all year · it is a roughly 17-room property starting at about THB 900–1,500/night · TripAdvisor ranks it #1 among B&B/Inn properties in Mae Chan district from 62 reviews.

body.html: Who Phumektawan Resort is for — the shortest way to put it: Phumektawan is a resort for people who genuinely want to escape the bustle of the city and stay up in nature on a mountaintop · it is not a fancy in-town hotel with a row of staff waiting to greet you, and it is not a five-star resort where everything is flawless · it is a small property on Doi Mae Salong (officially called Santikhiri) that sells quiet, cool air, and mountain-and-tea-plantation views you never get tired of · it sits in Mae Salong Nok subdistrict, Mae Fa Luang district, Chiang Rai, at an altitude of around 1,300 meters, which keeps the air cool and comfortable nearly all year and properly cold late in the year · from real reviews across several platforms, the people who fit best here are couples who want a quiet, romantic atmosphere, families bringing parents or kids up for the fresh air, and nature travelers who come specifically to watch the sea of mist, sip tea, and visit the tea plantations of Doi Mae Salong · those who may not fit are people expecting five-star luxury, wanting every amenity on hand, or not comfortable driving up steep mountain roads, because the focus here is simplicity and nature · TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 7 B&B/Inn properties in Mae Chan district, which reflects that among local stays in this area, Phumektawan does well and is remembered fondly by people who have stayed.

Location and getting there — Phumektawan sits at 86 Moo 6, Ban Mae Salong Nok, Mae Salong Nok subdistrict, Mae Fa Luang district, on the slopes of Doi Mae Salong · from the resort it is about 3 kilometers to the center of Santikhiri village and the Mae Salong market, and about 3.7 kilometers to Wat Mae Salong · the thing to be clear about is that Doi Mae Salong is a fair distance from the city of Chiang Rai, around 1.5–2 hours by car, and about 29 kilometers from Mae Fah Luang–Chiang Rai Airport (CEI) as the crow flies, though the actual winding mountain road takes longer · the route up the mountain is paved but steep with many bends, and the final stretch before the resort is a turn up an incline that many reviews warn is fairly steep and narrow, so use a vehicle with good power or someone who is confident driving on mountain roads · if you are not comfortable driving in the hills, the advice is to hire a car with driver from the city of Chiang Rai, or use a songthaew/chartered ride up Doi Mae Salong · the upside of this location is that once you are up here, you are close to nearly all the main sights of Doi Mae Salong — the tea plantations, the royal chedi, and the sea-of-mist viewpoints — so the resort makes a convenient base for exploring the mountain · one more thing to note is that after dark the mountain is fairly deserted with few streetlights, so plan to reach your room before nightfall for safety and to find the resort entrance more easily.

"I opened the door in the morning and there was the sea of mist and the tea plantations right in front of me. The air was so cold I had to put on a jacket · the road up is a bit steep but once you're there it's worth it for the view. The owner was really kind too."

Room types and decor — Phumektawan is a small resort of around 17 rooms, laid out in separate buildings stepping down the hillside, so many rooms get full mountain and tea-plantation views · the room types found on booking channels range from standard king rooms and superior family rooms to upper-floor rooms with wider open views and bungalows · the decor is a simple mountain-resort style, warmed up with woodwork and natural tones — not luxurious, but clean and comfortable · the standout feature of the rooms is the private balcony where you can sit and take in the mountains and sea of mist straight from your room, which reviews often call the best value of all · in-room amenities cover the basics for a mountain stay, such as a fan, TV, and a sofa sitting area · to be honest, hot water and heating are the points reviews flag to watch — some reviews note that a few rooms aren't warm enough or the water heater isn't very strong, which matters on a cold mountain · so if you come in the cold season, ask about hot water and request extra blankets at check-in · another point some older reviews mention is the attention to certain details and door locks in some rooms, which is the nature of a small mountain stay and something to set expectations around for the price level · overall, if you see it as an affordable mountain-view resort, the rooms deliver views and atmosphere that are worth the money.

Facilities, viewpoint, and atmosphere — the highlight that makes Phumektawan memorable is the 360° restaurant and viewpoint that looks out over mountain ridges, valleys, and terraced tea plantations in every direction · the early-morning hours are the most beautiful, because you have a chance to see the sea of mist floating below with the first light of day — a scene many reviews cite as the main reason they chose to stay here · the resort has gardens and photo spots scattered around, perfect for a morning or evening stroll in the cool air · the basic facilities include free parking, free Wi-Fi, a restaurant, a cafe, room service, luggage storage, and a reception counter · you have to understand this is a mountain resort, so there is no swimming pool, fitness room, or in-town hotel spa — and most people who come don't expect those anyway, because the charm here is the quiet, fresh air, and natural views · one note on Wi-Fi: some reviews say the signal up the mountain isn't very stable, which is normal for mountainous areas, so if you need to work online during your stay, set your expectations accordingly · the overall atmosphere suits a slow getaway — reading a book, sipping tea, and watching the view — more than looking for activities at the resort.

Food and the restaurant — Phumektawan's restaurant serves Thai food and Yunnanese Chinese food, the local cuisine of the Thai-Chinese community on Doi Mae Salong · the point many reviews agree on is that the food is good and the owner is kind, especially Yunnanese dishes like stewed pork leg with mantou buns, pork belly with pickled greens, and dishes that use tea leaves as an ingredient, which are hard to find outside this area · breakfast is included in the room rate, and many reviews say it comes in generous, filling portions, eaten while taking in the view — the most blissful part of staying here · there is also a cafe for sipping coffee or Mae Salong tea with the afternoon view · because it is a small resort, the menu isn't as extensive as a big hotel, and dining options on the mountain in the evening are limited, so eating dinner at the resort is the most convenient choice, but you should give notice in advance if you plan to dine here so the kitchen can prepare in time · anyone who wants to try more local food can head down to the restaurants in Santikhiri village or the tea shops in the Mae Salong market during the daytime · overall, food is a strong point that impresses people and gets mentioned among the top things in reviews here.

Service — service is another point that earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews · what's mentioned most often is that the owner and staff are friendly and helpful — many reviews recount the owner recommending places to visit, sea-of-mist viewpoints, and restaurants on the mountain, making it feel more like staying at a relative's house than a hotel · it is a warm, family-run resort, so you get a level of care you won't find at chain hotels · but to be straight, there are some voices in the reviews with a different take, such as reception that isn't always consistent and English communication with foreign guests that is still limited · also, the reception counter keeps set hours (around 7:00 AM–7:00 PM), so if you arrive late, let them know your check-in time in advance so someone is there to receive you · overall, service is still a strong point and the reason many people say they'd come back.

Voices from real reviews (the good and the critical) — pulling from TripAdvisor, Agoda, Trip.com, and Wongnai, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the gorgeous mountain and tea-plantation views, especially the morning sea of mist; the 360° restaurant; cool comfortable weather year-round; good food, particularly the Yunnanese dishes; a friendly owner and staff; clean rooms and comfortable beds; and the quiet that suits a restful stay · On the things to watch side: the most-mentioned is the steep, narrow road up the mountain, which requires a powerful vehicle and a driver comfortable on hill roads · next is hot water in some rooms that isn't strong or warm enough on very cold nights, an unstable Wi-Fi signal as the mountain terrain dictates, limited English communication, and some recent reviews reporting noise at night or certain meals not to their taste · to be fair, it must be stressed that review scores differ from platform to platform — TripAdvisor gives it around 4.3 out of 5 (#1 of B&B/Inn in Mae Chan from 62 reviews), which is high, but some platforms with fewer reviews score it lower · this difference reflects that the experience depends on the room you get, the time you go, and each person's expectations, more than a fixed standard, so setting your expectations to "a small, affordable mountain resort" will help you enjoy the stay more.

"The food was really good, the Yunnanese menu was excellent, and the owner was friendly and fun to chat with · the only catch was that the night we went the hot water wasn't very strong, and with the cold air it made showering a bit hard. Next time I'll ask about the hot water before booking."

Price and value — Phumektawan's room rates are in the accessible range, starting at about THB 900–1,500/night in regular season, and they may climb during the cold-season high season (November–January) when crowds head up the mountain for the sea of mist and the cold air · compared with other stays on Doi Mae Salong, this price is good value among budget mountain-view resorts, especially once you count the tea-plantation and sea-of-mist views you get from the rooms and the 360° restaurant, plus the included breakfast · anyone looking for a luxury five-star stay on the mountain may have to look elsewhere and pay several times more, but if the goal is fresh cool air, the views, and local food on a comfortable budget, Phumektawan offers good value · the tip is to compare prices across several platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com), because rates for small resorts often vary by season and promotion, and sometimes booking directly with the resort may get you a better price or more flexible terms.

Things to know before booking — several things help make the stay smoother · one, getting there matters most — the road up the mountain and into the resort is steep and narrow, so use a vehicle with good power, and if you're not comfortable driving in the hills, hire a driver or rent a car with driver from the city of Chiang Rai, and try to arrive before nightfall because the mountain is dark with few streetlights · two, if you come in the cold season, bring enough warm clothing, because at 1,300 meters the air really is cold, and ask about hot water and request extra blankets at check-in · three, to see the sea of mist, wake up before dawn and check the weather forecast — the best chances are in the cold season and right after fresh rain · four, give notice of your check-in time in advance because the counter keeps set hours, and if you'll eat dinner at the resort, tell the kitchen ahead · five, set your expectations around Wi-Fi and phone signal that may be unstable on the mountain — take it as a chance to unplug from screens · six, book ahead during the cold-season high season because stays on Doi Mae Salong are limited and fill up fast.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Phumektawan Resort is the best fit for people who want to stay among the mountain, tea-plantation, and sea-of-mist views on Doi Mae Salong, on a budget they can manage · its strengths are the 360° views, cool comfortable weather year-round, tasty local Yunnanese food, and a friendly, attentive owner · if you're looking for five-star luxury, every amenity on hand, strong hot water in every room, and you don't want to risk driving up steep mountain roads, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a stay in the city of Chiang Rai or a luxury resort on another mountain instead · but for a nature trip where you want to wake up to a sea of mist, sip Mae Salong tea, and get close to the Santikhiri community's way of life, with warm family-run service — Phumektawan is a worthwhile, memorable choice, and the reason it still holds a place in the hearts of people who love Doi Mae Salong.

honestSummary: Phumektawan Resort is the best fit for people who want to stay among the mountain, tea-plantation, and sea-of-mist views on Doi Mae Salong on a manageable budget — 360° views, cool air year-round, and tasty local Yunnanese food · but you have to accept that the road up is steep, it's a small resort with simple facilities, and details like hot water and Wi-Fi are points to plan around.
honestChecks: If you're not comfortable driving up mountains — the road up the mountain and into the resort is steep and narrow → hire a driver or rent a car with driver from the city of Chiang Rai, and arrive before nightfall.

If you come in the cold season and feel the cold — at 1,300 meters the air really is cold and hot water in some rooms isn't strong → bring warm clothing, ask about hot water, and request extra blankets at check-in.
If you want five-star luxury and every amenity — this is a small mountain resort focused on views and nature → consider a luxury stay on another mountain or in the city of Chiang Rai instead.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Phumektawan Resort, Doi Mae Salong

faq.q: Where is Phumektawan Resort · how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is at 86 Moo 6, Ban Mae Salong Nok, Mae Salong Nok subdistrict, Mae Fa Luang district, Chiang Rai province, on Doi Mae Salong (Santikhiri) at an altitude of around 1,300 meters · it's about 3–3.7 km from Santikhiri village and Wat Mae Salong, and about 29 km from Mae Fah Luang–Chiang Rai Airport (a 1.5–2 hr drive up the mountain) · the road up is steep and narrow, so use a vehicle with good power or hire a driver, and arrive before nightfall.

faq.q: Can you see the sea of mist at Phumektawan · when is it most beautiful?
faq.a: Yes · the highlight here is the 360° restaurant and viewpoint looking out over the mountains, tea plantations, and the morning sea of mist · the best chances to see the sea of mist are in the cold season (November–January) and right after fresh rain — wake up before sunrise and check the weather forecast.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Phumektawan · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 900–1,500/night in regular season · there are Standard King, Superior Family, upper-floor (Superior Upper Floor), and bungalow rooms · cold-season high-season rates climb and stays fill up fast, so book ahead and compare across platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com).

It's a great fit for couples, families, and nature travelers who want to stay among the mountain and sea-of-mist views on Doi Mae Salong on a manageable budget · it has 360° views, cool air year-round, and tasty local Yunnanese food · if you're looking for five-star luxury or aren't comfortable driving up the mountain, a stay in the city of Chiang Rai may suit you better.

faq.q: What are the hot water and cold weather like at Phumektawan?
faq.a: At an altitude of around 1,300 meters, the air is cool year-round and properly cold late in the year · some reviews note that hot water in certain rooms isn't very strong on very cold nights, so we recommend you bring warm clothing, ask about hot water, and request extra blankets at check-in.

faq.q: Does Phumektawan have food and a restaurant?
faq.a: Yes · the restaurant serves Thai food and Yunnanese Chinese food, the local cuisine of Doi Mae Salong, and reviews praise the taste and the kind owner · breakfast is included in the room rate · evening dining on the mountain is limited, so give the kitchen notice in advance if you'll eat dinner at the resort.
